newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Yugoslav army stance on protests.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Yugoslav army stance on protests.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday welcomed as a "significant development" a Yugoslav military leader's statement that the army would stay out of the stand-off between the opposition and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
"We view that as a positive announcement," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said.
"We commend recent statements by military officials that they will remain neutral in the confrontation and will refuse to use violence against peaceful protesters."
Gen. Momcilo Perisic, chief of the Yugoslav army general staff, told a student delegation on Monday that under the constitution the army stayed out of politics.
He said he favoured a democratic solution to the crisis which would help Yugoslavia rejoin Europe.

"We'll have to see what it means, but when you get the armed forces as in this case indicating that they'll remain neutral in the confrontation, that's very significant and a very positive development," Davies told a news briefing.

Protesters have been demonstrating for more than seven weeks in Belgrade, demanding that Milosevic's socialists respect the results of local elections that the opposition Zajedno coalition appeared to have won.

Davies said Washington was repeating its call on the Serbian government to accept immediately the results of the Nov. 17 elections, to open a meaningful dialogue with the opposition and to allow media freedom.
